summary: Jackson County, IL, Shawnee NF steel tower on Fountain Bluff, planned August 1934, 60 ft, manned from Camp Glenn; 1975 foundation noted; dismantled by 1985 per Wikipedia.

facts.design: Steel lookout tower with observation station (1934 announcement)
facts.status_note: Reported dismantled as of 1985 (Wikipedia). A 1975 survey note found an old concrete foundation and portions of an old tower in the area.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Shawnee National Forest

access.note: The hill is Shawnee National Forest land apart from a small private portion (Wikipedia). No source describes the summit or any remains there today.

events.note: August 27, 1934: a steel lookout tower and observation station reported as to be erected on Big Hill (Fountain Bluff)
Forest Service employees from Camp Glenn staffed the station; six fires put out from November 1 to November 16, 1934
Six forest fires extinguished from November 1, 1934; most reported from the lookout station
April 1936: a C.C.C. Camp Glenn worker stationed at the tower was taken seriously ill on duty and later returned to his position
310 visitors to the tower in the month before April 15, 1936
June 1949: vandals damaged picnic tables and fireplaces in the fire tower area on top of Fountain Bluff
National Geodetic Survey recovery note: survey mark not found; an old concrete foundation and portions of an old tower were found in the area
Reported dismantled as of 1985 (Wikipedia); no removal date given in these sources

notes_for_editor: Source 1 transcribes 1934, 1936 and 1949 newspaper items, a c.1942 listing, and an NGS datasheet. The newspapers and the NGS record were not read directly. The 1975 NGS note is the most recent description of physical remains found; no source describes the site today. Wikipedia's 'dismantled as of 1985' cites an unnamed reference not read, so treat that date as secondhand. The 60-foot height from the c.1942 listing matches the record's height_m 18.3. The 1934 article describes the tower as to be erected; the story says it was operating by November 1934 based on the fires reported from the lookout station. The 'access public' value reflects land status only. No new photos found.
